title: Subtoken prefetch and routing fragility - case notes
content:
Summary:
These notes capture a focused set of experiments investigating an observable class of tail-latency spikes and routing imbalance that manifests on long-context MoE workloads when tokenization boundaries produce many short subtoken runs. Hypothesis: subtoken fragmentation interacts poorly with our prefetch + gating handshake, causing uneven expert fanout and premature KV prefetch churn which amplifies GPU memcopy stalls on multi-arch setups (A100/H100).

Why this matters:
- Customer impact observed in a staging workload: 99th pctl generation latency increased 2-3x on long prompts (8k+) compared to baselines despite similar throughput.
- Symptoms: occasional single-request latency spikes (50–200ms extra), SLO violations for canary routes, transient OOM-like eviction behavior on 80GB GPUs (page-fault patterns).

Models and stacks tested:
- Llama-2-13B (fp16, kv-cache on GPU) on A100-80GB
- Mistral-7B (fp16, fused attention kernels) on H100-80GB
- Qwen-7B (mixed precision path) on A100
- Internal MoE prototype built from Llama-2-13B shard + 8-expert gating shim (deterministic top-2)
- Runtime: redwood-runtime v0.68 (experimental prefetch change), CUDA 12.1, cuDNN and custom kernels enabled

Repro commands (minimal):
- baseline generation trace:
  ./redwood-bench gen --model llama-13b --context 8192 --batch 1 --tokens 512 --profile perf.json
- moeroute stress test (mixed subtokens):
  ./redwood-bench gen --model moe-llama-13b --context 32768 --batch 4 --tokens 1024 --subtoken-fract 0.78 --profile moe_trace.json
Notes: --subtoken-fract is an experiment-only flag that injects fragmentary runs to emulate dense subtokenization boundaries observed on certain tokenizers.

Key observations (ordered rough chronology):
1) Prefetch timing windows misaligned with gated selection when subtokens are short:
   - When an input has many short subtokens (e.g., lots of punctuation, code), the runtime issues prefetches for the predicted expert KV ranges frequently. Because the gating decision comes slightly later in our current pipeline, we sometimes prefetch ranges that are then NOT used or are used for a smaller fanout than anticipated.
   - Cost: wasted PCIe/DMA bandwidth, eviction pressure on GPU LRU, and increased memcpy contention.

2) Fanout variance correlates strongly with subtoken-run-length distribution:
   - Collected gating logs across 10k requests: stdev(fanout) spikes by 2.1x for inputs with median subtoken length < 3.
   - Requests with high fanout variance show higher inter-expert synchronization waits in traces (per-expert lock waits).

3) Long-context exacerbates KV cache churn:
   - For 16k+ contexts the KV cache occupancy becomes fragmented. Prefetches for earlier positions are evicted as new ones arrive if the kernel scheduling doesn't prioritize in-window accesses. We saw LRU eviction events interleaved with prefetches in cuda-memlog.

4) Multi-arch differences:
   - H100 shows higher tolerance to memcpy contention due to improved DMA concurrency, but still suffers when the prefetch rate exceeds a threshold (measured ~6.5GB/s sustained per-GPU).
   - A100 setups flood the DMA engine sooner and we observe increased kernel stalls and occasional UVM evictions when multiple models are co-located.

Quantitative snippets (representative):
- Baseline (Llama-13B, A100, context=8192, batch=1): p50 78ms, p95 132ms, p99 210ms
- Fragmented run (MoE prototype, A100, context=32768, batch=4, subtoken-fract=0.78): p50 340ms, p95 780ms, p99 1240ms, with 14% of requests showing an extra 150–400ms memcpy stall in trace
- Measured DMA bandwidth during spikes: transient peaks 7.2–9.8GB/s per device (sustained baseline ~4.0GB/s)
- KV cache hit ratio drop: from 0.86 to 0.59 on fragmented inputs for long-context MoE workload

Profiling artifacts and where to look:
- perf.json / moe_trace.json flamegraphs: look at prefetch kernels (prefetch_kv_async), gating decision timer, and memcpy peaks.
- cuda-memlog shows alternating prefetch/evict patterns; timestamps align with gating jitter (~2–10ms jitter window).
- Traces: per-expert wait histograms show tail-rates dominated by small-number-of-experts being used heavily while many others are prefetched and idle.

Short-term mitigations tested (and results):
- Delay prefetch by gating-confidence window (added 6ms): reduced wasted prefetch bandwidth by ~48% and p99 improved ~22% on fragmented runs. Tradeoff: slightly increased p50 (4–8ms).
- Conservative fanout cap for inputs with median subtoken len < 4: reduced stdev(fanout) and eliminated worst OOM-like evictions at cost of ~6% throughput on favorable inputs.
- Opportunistic local cache promote: when prefetch load high, promote recently-used KV pages to a pinned region (experimental), reduced eviction rate by ~35% but increased pinned memory footprint which can cause denial of allocation for very large contexts.

Longer-term suggestions (prioritized):
1) Rework handshake: compute gating early (tokenization boundary precompute) so prefetch targets are known before heavy DMA scheduling. This requires moving a light-weight gate heuristic earlier in the pipeline and may require tokenizer/runtime co-design.
2) Subtoken-aware fanout heuristics: lower initial fanout when fragmentation is high and grow speculatively if gating confirms. Adaptive fanout saved cycles in the experiments.
3) KV prefetch batching: coalesce adjacent prefetch ranges across requests in the same scheduling window to amortize DMA cost. Need to measure cross-request latency amplification risk.
4) Scheduler QoS on DMA: enforce a soft cap on sustained prefetch bandwidth to match device thresholds (A100 vs H100 configured separately).
5) Improve observability: add subtokens-per-request histogram to per-route dashboards and a per-request prefetch/evict timeline in trace UI. This will make diagnosis easier for customers seeing spikes.

Open questions / unknowns to validate:
- Are certain tokenizers (e.g., code-style vs natural language) more likely to trigger this? Early signal points to byte-pair tokenizers on dense punctuation being the worst offenders. Need larger corpus run.
- How does mixed-precision quantization interact? We saw slight differences between fp16 and AMP paths in evacuation behavior—unclear if it's kernel scheduling or memory layout.
- Does MoE gating topology (top-1 vs top-2, deterministic vs stochastic) materially change prefetch patterns? Our quick tests show top-2 increases fanout variance which amplifies the issue.

Action items (who/when):
- Run corpus-scale sweep across 50k real-user prompts (Mariana, ETA 2026-02-20) to map tokenizer frag rates and correlate with production spike signals. (Linked: MLINFRA-8712)
- Prototype early-gating RFC and perf measurement (Ravi, branch run/exp-gate-early, ETA 2026-03-05).
- Add per-request subtoken histogram to trace payload (Noah, small telemetry PR #1427 already drafted).
- Follow-up infra test: run A100 vs H100 stress with pinned-memory promotion toggled (Ava + SRE, 2-day soak).

Notes to self / rough logs:
- Slack thread: thread:CB12345: see user reports 2026-01-19 for a canary that regressed after v0.68 rollout.
- Quick hack that helped: if (median_subtoken_len < 3) set fanout_cap=ceil(fanout_cap*0.6). Ugly but reduced worst-case mem churn.

Appendix (diagnostic snippets):
- Example trace excerpt (timestamps ms relative):
  0.0 token ingest
  1.8 prefetch_kv_async(rangeA) // speculative
  3.0 prefetch_kv_async(rangeB)
  3.6 gating_decision computed -> selected experts A,C
  4.2 cancel_prefetch(rangeB) // not always fast-cancelled, often still completes
  6.4 memcpy stall observed on compute thread (150ms)

- Helpful commands:
  nvprof --profile-from-start off --csv --log-file nvprof.csv 
  redwood-trace inspect moe_trace.json --span prefetch_kv_async --dump-timeline > pf_timeline.txt

If you want to reproduce a noisy instance quickly: run the moeroute stress test above with --subtoken-fract 0.78 and watch perf.json flamegraph. The pattern is visible after ~200 requests.

If this resonates with anyone who has seen similar: please add notes below or link to PRs/bugs. I want to consolidate heuristics into a single runtime flag set (prefetch.mode=adaptive) by the end of Q2 2026.

-- Ava
